## Objective
- Build a complete, playable offline mobile tactical FPS inspired by Counter-Strike 2.

## Requirements
- Build now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Support mobile play and offline use; check the game in screenshots saved as small JPEGs.

## Decisions
- Created an original single-player game called DUSTLINE rather than reproducing Counter-Strike 2 assets or branding.
- Implemented a self-contained raycast FPS with procedural graphics and no external gameplay assets; added a service worker for offline caching.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built a playable 5-hostile mission with movement, aiming, shooting, reloads, enemy attacks, health/armor, minimap, win/loss screens, and restart.
- Added desktop keyboard/mouse controls and mobile joystick, touch-look, and fire/reload controls.
- Added PWA manifest, icon, and offline service worker.
- Started the local server and checked desktop and phone-sized views; confirmed firing can neutralize an enemy.

### Active
- Final verification and any polish still needed.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the latest `screenshots/latest.jpg` if visual verification is needed.
2. Run a fuller gameplay check, including reload, enemy damage, and win/loss completion.
3. Check `git status` and report the changes as uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game interface and PWA registration.
- `game.js`: Raycast rendering, gameplay, bots, controls, HUD, and match flow.
- `style.css`: Desktop/mobile styling.
- `sw.js`: Offline asset caching.
- `manifest.webmanifest`: Installable app metadata.
- `icon.svg`: App icon.
- `screenshots/latest.jpg`: Most recent visual check.

## Important Context
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- A Playwright test started the match and fired once; the HUD showed `1 / 5` hostiles neutralized.
- The browser initially reported a missing `/favicon.ico`; an SVG favicon was subsequently added.

<subagent sessionID="ses_e24b883c3ffe8Goz1dWSj0FhIu" state="completed">
## Findings

- **Real dual-touch conflict — releasing the look finger can stop held fire.** On mobile, a touch that starts on the canvas is handled by the touch-look listeners, but it also generates pointer events. If one finger is holding the fire button (`mouseDown = true`) and a second finger looks on the canvas, that second finger’s `pointerup` reaches the canvas handler and unconditionally sets `mouseDown = false`. Sustained fire therefore stops when the look finger is lifted, even while the fire finger remains down. See [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:21`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ) and [line 23]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ).

  **Minimal fix:** Scope the canvas `pointerup` reset to a mouse pointer that began firing on the canvas; the fire button already resets its own state on `pointerup` and `pointercancel`. For more robust handling, track the active fire pointer/source rather than sharing an unqualified boolean.

- **Look state is not cleared on touch cancellation.** `lookTouch` is cleared on `touchend`, but there is no `touchcancel` handler. A canceled touch can leave stale look state until another qualifying touch replaces it. This is a smaller robustness issue than the firing conflict. See [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:22`]( /home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js ).

  **Minimal fix:** Clear the matching `lookTouch` on `touchcancel`, just as on `touchend`.

## Otherwise

- The joystick uses its own pointer ID and pointer capture, so its movement and release handling are separated from canvas touch-look. The fire button also has its own pointer release/cancel handlers.
- On a typical narrow mobile-emulation viewport, the look listener can receive canvas touches while joystick and fire touches target their overlaid controls; the code’s touch-look threshold also ignores starts in the leftmost 42% of the screen.
- HUD overlays can intercept touches because they sit above the canvas, so a look drag started over those regions will not reach the canvas listener. That appears to be a coverage limitation rather than an event conflict.

This is a static code review; I did not run browser emulation.
